title: Python Introduction
summary: Python lets you give a computer steps to follow. Read a short program that says hello and adds numbers.
introduction: You can teach a computer a small task by writing a program. Python is one language for doing this. Its short commands make it a good place to start. We will read three tiny programs and see what each one shows. You do not have to understand a whole app at once.
learningObjectives: Explain why a Python program needs a Python tool
Read a program that saves a name and counts pencils

blocks.text: To run these examples on your computer, you need **Python 3**. A tool called the Python interpreter reads your code and carries out its steps. Ask an adult to help install it if needed. This site shows Python code and answers, but its Run button does not run Python.
`print` shows an answer on the screen. It does not send a page to a paper printer. Put your words inside quotes and put them inside the round brackets.
Python can add and subtract. Numbers do not need quote marks. It reads the first line, then the second line, so the answers appear in that order.

blocks.code:
name = "Mia"
pencils = 3
pencils = pencils + 2
print("Hello,", name)
print("Pencils:", pencils)
blocks.title: A small pencil counter

blocks.text: A **variable** is a name for a value. `name` holds the text `"Mia"`. `pencils` holds a number. The `=` sign saves the value on the right under the name on the left.

rows: A set of steps for a computer.
A tool that reads and runs Python code.
The answer or message a program shows.

blocks.title: Watch out
blocks.text: Quote marks must come in pairs. Write `print("Hello")`, with a quote on each side of Hello. Python 2 is an old version; use Python 3 for these lessons.

blocks.title: Your turn
blocks.text: On paper, change Mia to your name and 3 pencils to 6 pencils. What will the last two lines show? Check your guess with Python 3 if it is installed.

seo.title: Python Introduction – Install Python 3.13 and Run a Script
seo.description: Learn what Python is used for, install Python 3.13, run your first script from the terminal and explore the interactive prompt, with exact output.
